artworks.title: Potato Breathes Life
artworks.description: A crowned king cradles a potato close to his face as shadowed figures reach toward its warm glow. The intimate act of breathing and the public desire for illumination meet in a nearly monochrome amber devotional tableau.

artworks.title: Dragon Master King
artworks.description: A king rides a dark dragon through a vaulted hall while two children watch. Mythic supremacy is interrupted by a comic promise to return after an ordinary errand, creating an uneasy joke about presence and absence.

artworks.title: King Presents Holy Child
artworks.description: A crowned king raises a haloed child before a vast assembly; a figure in papal white is seen from behind. The image rearranges traditions of royal presentation and sacred infancy into a spectacle of public recognition.

artworks.title: Rent Free Tim Dooley
artworks.description: An amusement park queue and the sign RENT FREE TIM DOOLEY literalize the internet expression 'living rent-free in someone's head'. Mass enthusiasm, spectacle and self-satire share the same frame.

artworks.title: The Acquired King
artworks.description: A fictionalized intelligence control room displays a crowned figure and target-acquisition text. The image is political satire, not evidence of surveillance, a real operation or involvement by the named agency.

artworks.title: The Coronation of the Potato
artworks.description: A winged crowned figure holds a luminous potato amid a crowd. Sacred kingship and everyday food are compressed into one deliberately incongruous emblem.

artworks.title: The Riders Beyond the Window
artworks.description: Three readers study texts indoors as an enthroned rider appears in a radiant scene beyond the window. Study and vision occupy neighboring spaces without resolving what the observers understand.

artworks.title: The Fallen Son and the World Tree
artworks.description: A thorn-crowned giant lies across icy and volcanic terrain, roots and a cosmic tree rising from his body toward an Odin-like figure and ravens above. The arrangement juxtaposes sacrifice, seasonal renewal and Norse cosmic architecture.
